questions.title: A mature oocyte carries only an X chromosome
questions.subject: dev
questions.question: A normal mature human oocyte naturally contains which of the following sex chromosomes?

explanations.A: Incorrect. A mature oocyte can never carry a Y chromosome, because the female germline is XX from the outset, with no Y chromosome present to be segregated into any meiotic product.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 'Either X or Y' correctly describes the two possible outcomes of spermatogenesis, produced by an XY germline, but it does not describe oogenesis, which can only ever yield an X-bearing egg.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A single haploid gamete carries only one sex chromosome, never both simultaneously; this would also require an XY, not XX, starting germline.
explanations.D: Correct. Every primary oocyte begins meiosis with the XX sex-chromosome pair and no Y chromosome, so whichever sex chromosome ends up in the mature oocyte after meiosis can only ever be an X — making the fertilizing sperm, not the egg, the determinant of the conceptus's chromosomal sex. This is the direct converse of spermatogenesis, where an XY germline produces both X-bearing and Y-bearing sperm in equal numbers.

questions.learning_objective: State that a mature oocyte's sex chromosome is always X, never Y, because the female germline (XX) contains no Y chromosome to segregate.
